Judgment

1. Brief facts of this case are that on 28.11.2014, an information was received at 4:45 pm at PS Karawal Nagar regarding hanging of a lady at H.No. 96, Gali No.9, Phase-IV, O Block, Shiv Vihar,
Karawal Nagar, Delhi.
On the basis of said information, DD No. 27A (Ex.PW9/A) was recorded and the same was assigned to ASI Shiv Shankar.
Thereafter, ASI Shiv Shankar alongwith Ct. Manoj reached the spot where on the ground floor, one dead body of a lady was found lying.
Her name was revealed as Lakshmi.
A saree was tied with the ceiling fan and hanging.
Crime team was called.
SDM concerned was also informed.
Form No.25.35B was prepared at the spot.
Parents of the deceased lady were also informed.
A saree which was tied with the ceiling fan was removed and seized vide seizure memo Ex.PW3/A.
On 29.11.2014, the mother of Lakshmi, namely, Rajbala reached SDM Office.
Her statement was recorded in question and answer form.
She stated that deceased Lakshmi is her eldest daughter and besides the deceased, she has three more children - two boys and one girl.
The deceased Lakshmi was married with Satya Prakash @ Pintu on 02.12.2008 as per Hindu Rites and Ceremonies.
At the time of marriage, there was no demand of dowry from the side of groom.
The dowry articles were given by them out of their own will.

After the marriage, the relation of Fir No. 1083/2014 State vs . Satya Prakash Page 1 Of 27 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20817143/
1 deceased Lakshmi with her in-laws were cordial, however, the husband of deceased Lakshmi used to beat her and pressurize her to earn, which led to quarrel between them on many occasions.

The parents of the deceased tried to reason with the accused on many occasions, the accused would mend his ways for a brief period but after some time, the accused used to resume quarrel with her daughter.
Her daughter wants to live with her children but their son-in-law wanted her to do some job.
At about 5:30 pm, on the date before she has received phone call from the father-in-law of deceased, who stated that Lakshmi has hanged herself.
Upon hearing about this, when they reached there, they found that Lakshmi was lying dead in a bed and crowd was gathered there.
Some neighbours stated that Lakshmi came back at home at about 3:00 pm from work and their son-in- law came at about 4:00 pm.
After some time, the son-in-law again left home and when he returned after about one hour, he raised alarm stating that Lakshmi had hanged herself.
She has suspicion that her son-in-law might have killed her daughter.
On the basis of statement Ex.PW1/A, present FIR was registered.
On 30.11.2014, the post-mortem of the deceased Lakshmi was got conducted and after post-mortem, the dead body was handed over to the relatives.
The accused Satya Prakash was arrested.
COMMITTAL 2.
After completion of necessary formalities, charge-sheet was filed in the Court of Ld. Ilaqa MM.
After taking cognizance and compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C., the present case was committed to the Courts of Sessions.
CHARGE 3.

After hearing the arguments and upon finding that prima facie case is made out against the accused Satya Prakash for the offences punishable u/s 498A/304B of IPC, charge was framed by ld.
Predecessor against accused persons, to which accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, prosecution got examined as many as twelve witnesses.
PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4. (i) PW1 Raj Bala is the mother of the deceased.

She deposed that Laxmi was her eldest daughter,
who was married with accused Satya Prakash in the year 2008.
After the marriage, accused kept her daughter well just for sometime and thereafter he started beating her on the ground that she had not brought enough dowry.
He used to pressurize Laxmi to bring Rs.1 lac from her parents or to start working and earn herself.
On 28.11.2014 at about 5 pm, father of accused Satya Prakash called her on her mobile phone and informed that her daughter Laxmi had committed suicide by hanging herself.
She along with her husband and other family members went to the house of the accused at Shiv Vihar, where she found her daughter lying on a bed in dead condition.
Police was already there.
On 29.11.2014, SDM of the area recorded her statement Ex.PW1/A.

Next day i.e on 30.011.2014,
police came to her house and made inquiries from her.
She told the police that eight days prior to this incident, her daughter Laxmi had come to her house.
She was at that time having injuries on her head.
She(Laxmi) told her that accused Satya Prakash had given her beatings and had also snatched her mobile phone.
She also told that accused was raising demand of Rs.1 lac from her or to start working and earn the said amount herself.

Out of the wedlock of Satya Prakash and Laxmi, two issues, one son and one daughter, were born.
She deposed that they are presently with their grandparents.

During the subsistence of the marriage,
she had talked to accused Satya Prakash and tried to make him understand but all proved futile.
In her cross-examination, she affirmed that neither her nor her daughter lodged any complaint with the police against the accused and his family members.
Her daughter was working in some restaurant near the office of accused.
A compromise was reached between her daughter and accused at Indrapun address.
The witness had been shown an alleged settlement dated 14.02.2013 but the witness denied her signatures on the said settlement.
She did not remember if any settlement had been reached between her family and accused family on 14.02.2013.
She affirmed that a settlement had been reached between the two families at the residence of accused but she did not remember any date, month or year, however, it was winter.
She affirmed that she had not stated about the demand of Rs. 1 lac before the SDM as she was perplexed at that time.
She affirmed that her daughter was once admitted to Mavi Nursing Home Shanti Nagar, Loni.

sentences.text: She volunteered that after a quarrel had taken place between her daughter and the accused, she had visited Mavi Nursing Home on receipt of information that her daughter was admitted there.
She did not know the details/cause of the quarrel but her daughter had sustained injuries and due to that reason, she was admitted to the nursing home.
Her daughter had sustained injury on her arm/hand as she had seen her arm bandaged.
She affirmed that she did not lodge any complaint regarding her injury on that occasion.
She volunteered that since she wanted marriage of her daughter to survive.
After every quarrel/incident with the accused, her daughter always wanted them to take action against him.
She wanted them to lodge complaint against him and his family members but they always persuaded her not to do so and they always wanted her to get settled and her marriage to survive.
Accused always ill- treated her.
At times, he used to snatch her mobile phone.
At other times, he used to lock her inside the room before assaulting her.
She had told her about such things eight days before her death when she happened to visit them.
She had sent her to stay with accused though she did not want to go there.
She affirmed that she never told the police about the above-said conduct of the accused for the simple reason that she wanted to survive her marriage.
She volunteered that with great difficulty, she had got her married.
She was working as maid in different houses.
She had to look after her three other children also.
For all these reasons, she always persuaded her daughter to bear with accused and stay with him.
She further deposed that she had seen that her daughter had sustained injury on her head but that was not so serious as to warrant medical treatment.

He volunteered that Mohit used to reside in the adjoining house of accused.
He was on visiting terms with accused.
His daughter therefore used to talk to said Mohit.
He affirmed that accused had asked him to advise his daughter that she should not speak to said Mohit.
He also affirmed that his daughter had herself broken her mobile phone in anger because accused had told her not to speak to Mohit.
He had enquired his daughter as to whether she had broken her mobile when she visited them and she confirmed.
Mohit used to call her daughter even when residence was shifted by the accused and accused never wanted her daughter to speak to him.
Her daughter got angry and she broke the mobile so that she did not receive any call from Mohit.
After the mobile was broken, there was no quarrel between her daughter and accused regarding Mohit.

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED 5.

After completion of prosecution evidence, the statement of accused Satya Prakash was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. wherein incriminating facts emerging from the prosecution evidence were put to the accused, which were denied by him.
He stated that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
Accused did not opt to lead evidence in defence.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 6.
This court has heard the arguments and perused the record.

It is submitted on behalf of accused that there are major contradictions and material improvements in the testimony of prime witnesses of the prosecution namely PW1 Smt. Rajbala (mother of the deceased) and PW2 Sh. Sunil Kumar (father of the deceased).
It is submitted that the deceased had committed suicide as she used to remain depressed for not being able to meet one Mohit with whom she was having an extramarital affair.
No complaint regarding harassment, demand of dowry or torture caused to the daughter of complainant has ever been made by the in-laws of the accused at any time prior to the date of incident.

The attention of the court was also drawn towards one settlement Ex. PW2/D1, arrived at between the relatives of bride side and the relatives of groom side on 14-02-2013, which was produced during the cross-examination of PW2 Sh. Sunil Kumar whereby it was agreed that if due to some reason, the bride commits any untoward incident then no accusations shall be leveled on Fir No. 1083/2014 State vs . Satya Prakash Page 1 Of 27 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20817143/
9
the groom side.

It is, therefore, prayed that benefit of doubt should be conferred upon the accused,
and accused be acquitted from all the charges.
On the other hand, Ld. Addl. PP for the State submits that the testimony of all the prosecution witnesses is sufficient to bring home the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubts.
The accused has not been able to rebut the statutory presumption u/s 113B of the Indian Evidence Act.
There is only bald suggestion, as reflected from cross-examination of PW2 indicating extramarital affair of deceased with one Mohit.
No call details record with regard to the telephonic conversations between the deceased and Mohit have been placed on record.
No defence evidence was led.
There is no material contradiction in the version of prime witnesses got examined by the prosecution.
FINDINGS OF THE COURT 7.

Before analyzing the prosecution and defence evidence adduced in the present case, this court deems it proper to refer to provisions of law, which are found to be applicable on the facts of the present case.

Sections 304B, 498A, 406 IPC and 113B Indian Evidence Act read as under:-
"304B. Dowry death--Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
498A.

Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty--Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation--For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

406--Punishment for criminal breach of trust--Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman has been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, on in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.

17.1. To attract the provisions of Section 304-B IPC the main ingredient of the offence to be established is that soon before the death of the deceased she was subjected to cruelty and harassment in connection with the demand of dowry.
17.2. The death of the deceased woman was caused by any burn or bodily injury or some other circumstance which was not normal.
17.3. Such death occurs within seven years from the date of her marriage.
17.4. That the victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband.
17.5. Such cruelty or harassment should be for or in connection with demand of dowry.
17.6. It should be established that such cruelty and harassment was made soon before her death.

sentences.text: (a) By and large a witness cannot be expected to possess a photographic memory and to recall the details of an incident.
It is not as if a video tape is replayed on the mental screen.
(b) Ordinarily it so happens that a witness is overtaken by events.
The witness could not have anticipated the occurrence which so often has an element of surprise.
The mental faculties therefore cannot be expected to be attuned to absorb the details.
(c) The powers of observation differ from person to person.
What one may notice, another may not.
An object or movement might emboss its image on one person's mind, whereas it might go unnoticed on the part of another.

They can only recall the main purport of the conversation.
It is unrealistic to expect a witness to be a human tape recorder.

(f) Ordinarily a witness cannot be expected to recall accurately the sequence of events which take place in rapid succession or in a short time span.
A witness is liable to get confused, or mixed up when interrogated later on.

(g) A witness, though wholly truthful, is liable to be overawed by the court atmosphere and the piercing cross-examination made by counsel and out of nervousness mix up facts, get confused regarding sequence of events, of fill up details from imagination on the spur of the moment.

The subconscious mind of the witness sometimes so operates on account of the fear of looking foolish or being disbelieved though the witness is giving a truthful and honest account of the occurrence witnessed by him perhaps it is a sort of psychological defence mechanism activated on the moment.

13. It has been held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Sonu Arora Vs. State on 21 July, 2010 in Crl. A. No. 241/1997 that:-
"If the discrepancies found in the testimony of a witness are normal and attributable to loss of memory with the passage of time or they are on matters which are peripheral or trivial, not forming the core of the case, his testimony cannot be rejected on account of such minor variations or infirmities.

But, where the contradiction relates to the main incident forming core part of his testimony, that could depending upon the nature of the contradiction and other facts and circumstances of the case, seriously affect the credibility and truthfulness of the witness since he is not expected to give contradictory version with respect to the important material parts of the incident which he claims to have witnessed."
